# GenevaERS Expert Review Session — May 2019

**Date:** May 2019  
**Type:** Recorded working session  
**Participants:** Kip Twitchell and GenevaERS/IBM colleagues (including Rick Roth)  
**Related deck:** [Shared Ledger Concepts.pptx](../../conceptual-model/presentations/Shared%20Ledger%20Concepts.pptx) *(members repo)*  
**Status:** Raw auto-generated transcript. Not a formal record or minutes.

---

## Context

This session was a pre-LFX expert review of Kip Twitchell's financial systems architecture work — specifically the Minimum Cost Curve concept and the case for event-based, detail-preserving ledger architectures. GenevaERS joined the Linux Foundation in May 2020; this review predates that by one year and represents the internal conceptual alignment work that preceded the open-source project launch.

The discussion covers:
- The trajectory of Kip's career from Price Waterhouse (with Rick Roth) through IBM's global banking practice
- Why CFO budget constraints prevent fundamental ledger re-architecture at large banks
- The Minimum Cost Curve: an isoquant graph showing the interior minimum between transaction-only and balance-only reporting configurations
- Historical computing cost curves (1964 to present) as the structural cause of aggregated ledger architecture
- Ledger innovation stagnation since Luca Pacioli (1494) contrasted with exponential technology change
- The personal ledger as a worked example: Quicken → Mint.com and what that transition means for shared categorization

GenevaERS community members and contributors are welcome to review this transcript as background for the conceptual model and as context for why the GenevaERS engine's high-throughput, detail-preserving processing architecture is directly relevant to the Sharealedger vision.
